scoreReasons: Tempo settlement is public on chain. Tempo charge receipts carry the transaction hash and session receipts the channelId, with a transaction hash only when a settlement or close happens on chain.
MPPscan indexes servers, agents, transactions and volume, and its stats endpoint is public.
The mpp.dev services directory is public JSON.

Challenges, credentials and receipts are exchanged between client and server over TLS and are not published. Servers pass SPTs to Stripe and card credentials to their Server Enabler, and a Tempo credential's signed transfer becomes public once broadcast. SPT and card payments stay with the parties, their processors, the card networks and issuers.
The specs define no .well-known path and discovery documents are optional and unauthenticated.

public.how: TIP-20 transfers and escrow calls (open, settle, topUp, close, requestClose, withdraw); receipt reference is the transaction hash or channelId.
timeframeDays 0 (all time), 1, 7, 15 or 30; the homepage shows 7 days by default.
Public JSON listing 138 services and their methods on 2026-10-21 (tempo 135, stripe 10, evm 1).
Top-level x-service-info and per-operation x-payment-info (intent, method, amount, currency).
TIP-20 TransferWithMemo logs, which mppx reads to verify subscription settlement.

public.where: GitHub tempoxyz/mpp-specs and wevm/mppx; IETF Datatracker
public.how: Commits, pull requests, advisories and draft revisions.

private.why: Not published: exchanged between client and server over TLS and passed only to the payment processors a method names (card enablers, Stripe); credentials must never be logged. A Tempo credential's signed transfer becomes public once it is broadcast.

SPT card payments appear in the seller's Stripe API and Dashboard and are otherwise visible only to Stripe, the card networks and the issuer. Stablecoin payments to Stripe deposit addresses also settle on the public Tempo or Solana ledger, although the address does not name the seller.

private.what: Card authorizations through the card method
private.why: Not public. The network token is encrypted from the Client Enabler to the Server Enabler. The server sees the authorization reference and the plaintext card details in the credential (network, last four digits, expiry, billing address, cardholder name, payment account reference), and the enablers, network and issuer see the authorization.
Off-chain; only the newest settled amount reaches the chain.

Billing-period state and cancellation effective times are held by the server, and the specs define no public subscription registry. For Tempo subscriptions, the access-key registration with its limits and expiry, each period's transfer and any key revocation happen on chain.
